findings.title: Substring match misclassifies negated error queries as error-focused, inflating counts
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query checks `"event.type:error" in query`, a raw substring test on the lowercased query string. A discover query that explicitly EXCLUDES errors, e.g. `!event.type:error`, still contains the substring, so the function returns True and `count()` gets rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)`. The query then runs against events with no/NULL sample_weight, producing wrong (likely near-zero or otherwise incorrect) counts. The check must parse the query's filters rather than substring-match, or at minimum not match negated (`!`/`-` prefixed) conditions.

findings.title: Upsampling decision is computed from the closure dataset and raw request query, not the query actually executed
findings.body: Inside `_get_event_stats`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` uses the outer `dataset` module and `request.GET['query']`. But `_get_event_stats` is invoked by the dashboard-split path (`get_event_stats_factory.fn`) with a different `scoped_dataset` (e.g. `discover`) and a rewritten query string such as `({query}) AND !event.type:transaction`. For example, when the request dataset is `metrics_enhanced_performance` and the widget split re-routes an errors-only query to `discover`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` evaluates the metrics dataset and returns False, so an errors-only query is NOT upsampled even though the same query on the errors dataset would be. The eligibility check should receive `scoped_dataset` and the actual `query` argument being executed, not the closure variables.

findings.title: sum(sample_weight) has no NULL fallback; events lacking sample_weight silently count as zero
findings.body: The `upsampled_count` SnQL aggregate is `toInt64(sum(Column("sample_weight")))`. In ClickHouse, `sum` ignores NULLs, so any event in an allowlisted project whose `sample_weight` is not populated (events ingested before this feature rolled out, or events where the `error_sampling` context was absent) contributes 0 to the count. Once a project is added to the allowlist, its historical/unmarked events vanish from counts. There is no `coalesce(sample_weight, 1)` fallback, and the PR contains no production ingestion change that populates `sample_weight` — the only code that derives it is a test factory hack (`_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` in sentry/testutils/factories.py), suggesting the column may be NULL for real data. This silently undercounts errors.

findings.title: Global store_event factory change made solely to support this feature's tests, with dead exception handling
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` now runs for every `store_event` call in the entire test suite, mutating `sample_rate` on normalized data whenever an `error_sampling` context is present. This changes shared factory behavior for all other tests to support one feature's endpoint tests. Additionally, the `try/except Exception` around chained `.get()` calls is dead code (dict.get does not raise), and the try/except around `float()` silently swallows bad values. The fact that a factory hack is needed also indicates the production ingestion path that should populate `sample_weight` is not part of this PR, so the endpoint tests validate test-injected data rather than the real pipeline.

findings.title: invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code with no caller, so allowlist changes lag up to 60 seconds
findings.body: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined and documented as the mechanism to keep the 60-second eligibility cache consistent when the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option changes, but nothing in this PR calls it (no option-update signal, receiver, or task wiring). Removing a project from the allowlist therefore leaves the endpoint serving inflated upsampled counts for up to 60 seconds after the configuration change. Either wire the invalidation into the option-change path or remove the unused function.

findings.title: Accidental nested repo/submodule committed at repository root
findings.body: This PR adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink pointing at the base commit (a5d2909), which looks like an accidentally committed nested clone of the repository itself. It is unrelated to the feature, will confuse tooling (git treats it as a submodule with no .gitmodules entry), and should not be merged.

findings.title: Top-events ordering and selected columns are not transformed, only the timeseries columns
findings.body: When upsampling is enabled, only `y_axes`/`timeseries_columns` are rewritten to `upsampled_count() as count`, but `orderby=self.get_orderby(request)` and `selected_columns=self.get_field_list(organization, request)` are passed through untouched. If the client orders by `count()` (the common case for top events), the top-N series selection is ranked on the un-upsampled raw count while the displayed series values are upsampled, so the chosen top events and their relative magnitudes can disagree with the charted values.

findings.title: upsampled_count declares result type "number" while count() is "integer"
findings.body: The `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is registered with `default_result_type="number"`, whereas `count()` uses "integer". The SnQL expression is wrapped in `toInt64`, so the actual values are integers, but downstream consumers (zerofill defaults, chart rendering, response meta result types) key off the declared result type and may treat the aliased `count` column as a float, producing inconsistent behavior compared to every other count-like aggregate. It should be "integer" for parity with count().

findings.title: Main entry point is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects and its caching are untested
findings.body: The test class covers only the private helpers (`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`) and the column transform. The public function `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` — including the cache-hit path, cache-miss population, the 60-second TTL, and the combination of the cached allowlist result with the dataset/query check — has no test coverage, despite `setUp` constructing `self.snuba_params` and `self.request` specifically for it (both are then unused). `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is also untested. Since caching is the riskiest part of this change, it needs direct tests.

findings.title: Test comments contradict the asserted values in the upsampling tests
findings.body: In `test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects`, the assertions read `assert data[0][1][0]["count"] == 10  # First bucket has 1 event` and the same for the second bucket. The comments say the bucket has 1 event while the assertion checks the upsampled value of 10 (1 event at client_sample_rate 0.1). A reader will misread the expected behavior; the comments should state that each bucket has 1 stored event upsampled to a weighted count of 10.
